# 1. Introduction

The video game industry has grown into one of the largest entertainment industries in the world, generating billions of dollars in annual revenue. However, not all games achieve commercial success. Some titles become global bestsellers while others perform poorly despite significant development costs and marketing efforts. Understanding the factors that contribute to a game’s success is therefore important for publishers, developers, and investors.

This project analyzes factors associated with commercial success in video games using logistic regression. A binary classification model is developed to predict whether a game becomes a “hit” based on critic scores, genre, platform, and release year. Logistic regression is an appropriate modeling technique because the response variable is binary, representing whether a game achieved at least one million global sales.

The objectives of this study are:

* To identify significant predictors of commercial success in video games
* To evaluate the effectiveness of logistic regression for classification
* To interpret how game characteristics influence the probability of becoming commercially successful

# 2. Data Set: Video Game Sales 2024


```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(pROC)
library(purrr)
library(MASS)
# Load data
vg <- read.csv("D:/Video Game Sales 2024.csv", header = T)

# Check column names
names(vg)

# Clean data and create target variable
vg_clean <- vg %>%
  mutate(
    release_year = year(mdy(Released)),
    hit = if_else(Global_Sales >= 1.0, 1L, 0L)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Global_Sales),
    !is.na(Critic_Score),
    !is.na(Genre),
    !is.na(Console),
    !is.na(Publisher),
    !is.na(Developer),
    !is.na(release_year),
    release_year >= 1980,
    release_year <= 2024
  )

```
```{r}
# Function to group rare categories
make_balanced_group <- function(x, y, min_hit = 20, min_nonhit = 20) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  y <- as.character(y)

  tab <- table(x, y)

  if (!"0" %in% colnames(tab)) {
    tab <- cbind(tab, "0" = 0)
  }

  if (!"1" %in% colnames(tab)) {
    tab <- cbind(tab, "1" = 0)
  }

  keep <- rownames(tab)[tab[, "0"] >= min_nonhit & tab[, "1"] >= min_hit]

  ifelse(x %in% keep, x, "Other")
}
vg_model <- vg_clean %>%
  mutate(
    genre_group = factor(make_balanced_group(Genre, hit)),
    console_group = factor(make_balanced_group(Console, hit)),
    publisher_group = factor(make_balanced_group(Publisher, hit)),
    developer_group = factor(make_balanced_group(Developer, hit)),
    hit = factor(hit, levels = c(0, 1))
  )

vg_model <- vg_model[
  ,
  c(
    "hit",
    "Critic_Score",
    "genre_group",
    "console_group",
    "publisher_group",
    "developer_group",
    "release_year"
  )
]
```

```{r}
# Check class balance
table(vg_model$hit)
prop.table(table(vg_model$hit))

#Split train/test data
set.seed(123)

train_index <- sample(
  1:nrow(vg_model),
  0.7 * nrow(vg_model)
)

train_data <- vg_model[train_index, ]
test_data  <- vg_model[-train_index, ]
```

# 2. Fit a logistic regression model with all predictors

```{r}
# Fit logistic regression model
mdl.full <- glm(
  hit ~ Critic_Score +
    genre_group +
    console_group +
    publisher_group +
    developer_group +
    release_year,
  data = train_data,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

# Model summary
summary(mdl.full)
```
The full model identifies fire year, species, diameter, CSV, neighbors within a 15 m distance, HEGYI, basal area of neighboring trees of the same species within a 15 m distance, and basal area of all neighboring trees within a 15 m distance as significant. The other non-significant predictors are removed.


# 3. Select the best subset of variables. Perform a diagnostic on the best model.  Perform all possible inferences you can think about.

```{r}
# Likelihood Ratio Test for Variable Selection
drop1(mdl.full, test="LRT")
```
Predictor selection was performed using single-term deletion likelihood ratio tests through the drop1() function in R. Each predictor was removed individually from the full logistic regression model and compared against the full model using likelihood ratio tests. Results indicated that all predictors significantly contributed to model fit, with all p-values below 0.001. Therefore, the full model was retained as the final logistic regression model.

```{r}
# Stepwise backward selection using AIC
mdl.best <- stepAIC(
  mdl.full,
  direction = "both",
  trace = TRUE
)

summary(mdl.best)
```

```{r}
# Fit candidate logistic models 
m1 <- glm(hit ~ Critic_Score + genre_group + release_year,
          data = train_data, family = binomial(link = "logit"))

m2 <- glm(hit ~ Critic_Score + genre_group + release_year + console_group,
          data = train_data, family = binomial(link = "logit"))

m3 <- glm(hit ~ Critic_Score + genre_group + release_year + console_group + publisher_group,
          data = train_data, family = binomial(link = "logit"))

models <- list(
  "Model 1: score + year + genre" = m1,
  "Model 2: add console" = m2,
  "Model 3: add publisher" = m3
)

model_selection <- map_dfr(names(models), function(nm) {
  mod <- models[[nm]]

  p <- predict(
    mod,
    newdata = test_data,
    type = "response"
  )

  roc_obj <- roc(
    response = test_data$hit,
    predictor = p,
    levels = c("0", "1"),
    quiet = TRUE
  )

  tibble(
    model = nm,
    parameters = length(coef(mod)),
    AIC = AIC(mod),
    validation_AUC = as.numeric(auc(roc_obj))
  )
})


print(model_selection)

# Choose final model: lowest AIC and highest validation AUC
final_model <- m3
test_data$prob_hit <- predict(final_model, newdata = test_data, type = "response")

```


```{r}
# Null model
mdl.null = glm(hit~1, family=binomial(), data=train_data)
# Compare null model vs best model
anova(mdl.best, mdl.null, test="LRT")
AIC(mdl.null, mdl.best)
```
The final logistic regression model was compared against the null model using a likelihood ratio test. The null model contained only an intercept term and no predictors.

Results indicated that the final model significantly improved model fit compared to the null model (p<0.001). Additionally, the final model produced substantially lower deviance and AIC values, demonstrating improved explanatory power.

These results indicate that critic score, genre, console, publisher, developer, and release year collectively contribute significantly to predicting whether a video game becomes commercially successful.
```{r}
residuals=data.frame(rstandard(mdl.best,type="pearson"), residuals(mdl.best, type="pearson"),
                residuals(mdl.best,type="deviance"), rstandard(mdl.best,type="deviance"))
names(residuals)=cbind("standardized", "Pearson", "deviance", "std. dev")
boxplot(residuals,  ylim = c(-5, 5))
```
The model fit can be examined using the residuals, where the majority of the data is falling in a range with standard residuals less than 2

```{r}

coef_table <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(coef(mdl.best)),
  Estimate = coef(mdl.best),
  Odds_Ratio = exp(coef(mdl.best)),
  row.names = NULL
)

ci_beta <- suppressMessages(confint(mdl.best))
ci_or <- exp(ci_beta)

inference_table <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(coef(mdl.best)),
  Estimate = coef(mdl.best),
  Odds_Ratio = exp(coef(mdl.best)),
  Lower_95_CI = ci_or[, 1],
  Upper_95_CI = ci_or[, 2],
  row.names = NULL
)

coef_table
inference_table
```

# 4. Use the new model to make predictions.

```{r}
# Predicted Probabilities
pred.prob <- predict(
  mdl.best,
  newdata = test_data,
  type = "response"
)
```


# 5. Use different pi_0 as a cut-off point and create a confusion table.
```{r}
cutoffs <- c(0.25, 0.40, 0.50, 0.60, 0.75, 0.85, 0.90)

cutoff_results <- data.frame(
  cutoff = cutoffs,
  accuracy = NA,
  sensitivity = NA,
  specificity = NA
)

for (i in seq_along(cutoffs)) {

  pred_class <- ifelse(pred.prob >= cutoffs[i], 1, 0)

  cm <- table(
    Predicted = factor(pred_class, levels = c(0, 1)),
    Actual = factor(test_data$hit, levels = c(0, 1))
  )

  print(paste("Cutoff =", cutoffs[i]))
  print(cm)

  TN <- cm["0", "0"]
  FP <- cm["1", "0"]
  FN <- cm["0", "1"]
  TP <- cm["1", "1"]

  cutoff_results$accuracy[i] <- (TP + TN) / sum(cm)
  cutoff_results$sensitivity[i] <- TP / (TP + FN)
  cutoff_results$specificity[i] <- TN / (TN + FP)
}

cutoff_results
```

# 9. Try the probit link and the identity links to model data. 

```{r}
# probit
mdl.probit <- glm(
  hit ~ Critic_Score +
    genre_group +
    console_group +
    publisher_group +
    developer_group +
    release_year,
  family = binomial(link = "probit"),
  data = train_data
)
summary(mdl.probit)

preds = predict(mdl.probit, newdata=test_data, type="response")
prop = 0.912
yy <- test_data$hit
yhat <- as.numeric(preds >prop)
confusion <- table(yy, yhat)
confusion


confusion[1,1]/(confusion[1,1]+confusion[1,2])
confusion[2,2]/(confusion[2,1]+confusion[2,2])
(confusion[1,1]+confusion[2,2])/(confusion[1,1]+confusion[1,2]+confusion[2,1]+confusion[2,2])
```

```{r}
# identity
mdl.identity <- try(
  glm(
    hit ~ Critic_Score +
      genre_group +
      console_group +
      publisher_group +
      developer_group +
      release_year,

    family = binomial(link = "identity"),
    data = train_data
  ),
  silent = TRUE
)
if (inherits(mdl.identity, "try-error")) {

  print("Identity link model failed to converge.")

} else {

  summary(mdl.identity)

  preds <- predict(
    mdl.identity,
    newdata = test_data,
    type = "response"
  )

  prop <- 0.5

  yy <- as.numeric(as.character(test_data$hit))

  yhat <- as.numeric(preds > prop)

  confusion <- table(yy, yhat)

  confusion

}

```
```


# 10. Which model works better for this data?

The probit model performs the best for this data, with specificity, sensitivity, and accuracy slightly higher on the validation set than the logistic link model. The identity model fails to find the correct starting values.
